definition: In 2022, 16.9% (1,620) of the 9,586 Brazilian industrial companies with 100 or more employees used artificial intelligence in their operations Among the companies that used AI, the areas of administration (73.8%), product project development (65.9%), processes, services and marketing (65.1%) were those that used it the most, followed by the areas of production (56.4%) and logistics (48.4%).
details: In 2022, 16.9% (1,620) of the 9,586 Brazilian industrial companies with 100 or more employees used artificial intelligence in their operations Among the companies that used AI, the areas of administration (73.8%), product project development (65.9%), processes, services and marketing (65.1%) were those that used it the most, followed by the areas of production (56.4%) and logistics (48.4%).

explainer.lead: This term describes how Brazilian industrial companies with at least 100 employees used artificial intelligence in 2022. Adoption was concentrated in administration and product development, but also appeared in production and logistics.

tiers.eli5: Imagine 100 large Brazilian industrial companies: about 17 used AI in 2022. Among those users, AI helped most often with office administration and designing products, somewhat like a smart assistant that can help with different jobs around the same company.
tiers.practitioner: An industrial AI project may sit in administration, product project development, processes, services, marketing, production, or logistics rather than only on the factory floor. When interpreting adoption figures, keep the denominators separate: 16.9% covers all surveyed companies, while the functional-area percentages cover only the 1,620 AI users.
tiers.paperLevel: For Brazilian industrial companies with at least 100 employees in 2022, adoption was p = 1,620 / 9,586 ≈ 16.9%. Conditional on adoption, reported use was 73.8% in administration, 65.9% in product project development, 65.1% in processes, services and marketing, 56.4% in production, and 48.4% in logistics. These figures describe one year and company size band; they do not establish usage intensity or causal effects.

explainer.example: In a group of 100 comparable companies, the 16.9% adoption rate corresponds to roughly 17 AI users. If those users matched the reported pattern, about 12 or 13 would use AI in administration, while about 8 or 9 would use it in logistics.

explainer.intuition: Industrial AI is not confined to machines on a production line. The 2022 figures show companies applying it across several business functions, with administrative and product-development work leading adoption.
howItWorks: Start with the 9,586 Brazilian industrial companies that had at least 100 employees.
Identify the 1,620 companies, or 16.9%, that used AI in their operations in 2022.
Within that adopter group, measure which business areas used AI.
Compare administration, product development, processes, services, marketing, production, and logistics using their reported percentages.
explainer.whyItMatters: The figures provide a snapshot of both how common industrial AI adoption was and where it was applied. They also show that looking only at production would miss much of its reported use.
misconceptions: The area percentages are not shares of all 9,586 companies; they apply only to the 1,620 AI users.
A 16.9% adoption rate does not mean that AI performed 16.9% of industrial work.
Industrial AI use includes administrative and commercial functions, not just robots or factory automation.
